title: Quito Named UNESCO's First World Heritage City
reason: Confirmed from multiple independent sources: the historic center of Quito, Ecuador was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List on 18 September 1978, together with the Historic Centre of Kraków, Poland — both cited repeatedly as the first historic city centers ever inscribed under the 1972 World Heritage Convention, part of the inaugural batch of 12 sites (which also included Galápagos, Yellowstone, Mesa Verde, Aachen Cathedral, etc.). UNESCO's own criteria for Quito cite the exchange between Spanish and indigenous cultures and its status as one of the best-preserved historic centers in Latin America, matching the description's claims about colonial architecture (16th-18th century) and living indigenous/Spanish traditions. Follow-up research also confirms decades of subsequent restoration investment (FONSAL fund created 1987 after earthquake damage, $41M IADB loan in early 2000s, $200M tourism-driven investment ~2000, $55M+ 2020-2024), matching the description's claim about the listing driving restoration investment. Minor note: the World Heritage Committee's 2nd session that made the decision ran 5-8 September 1978 in Washington DC per the official UNESCO archive page, while "18 September" is the date used almost universally in secondary/tertiary sources (Wikipedia, multiple anniversary retrospectives) as the formal declaration/publication date — this is a plausible session-vs-publication distinction, not a substantive discrepancy, so it does not change the verdict.

verifications.reason: Multiple independent, authoritative sources confirm: the historic center of Quito, Ecuador was inscribed by UNESCO as a World Heritage Site on September 18, 1978, in the same inaugural inscription batch (the first 12 sites ever listed) as the Historic Centre of Kraków, Poland. The official UNESCO World Heritage Centre listing (whc.unesco.org/en/list/2) describes Quito as having 'the best-preserved, least altered historic centre in Latin America' and cites criteria (ii) and (iv) — an important interchange of human values between Spanish and indigenous populations producing a unique architectural ensemble — matching the description's claims about colonial architecture and living indigenous/Spanish traditions. Wikipedia's Quito article independently corroborates the exact date, the joint inscription with Kraków, and the 'first' designation. The claim about subsequent decades of restoration investment in the old town is a well-documented, uncontroversial consequence widely reported (e.g., Casa de la Cultura/BID-funded old-town rehabilitation programs) and consistent with the rest of the record.

title: Filanbanco Bailout Triggers Systemic Banking Collapse
reason: Independently verified every material claim. Filanbanco, Ecuador's largest bank, was rescued/bailed out by the government in November 1998 (formal handover to the state via AGD on Dec 2, 1998), consistent with the description. Multiple independent sources describe the causal chain exactly as stated: the Filanbanco rescue caused sucre depreciation and capital flight that worsened system liquidity and led to the closure of Banco del Progreso, confirmed as the second-largest bank (by assets), which shut in March 1999. President Jamil Mahuad declared a bank holiday starting March 8, 1999 (initially framed as a short/5-day holiday, later extended until banks reopened March 15), then signed Executive Decree 685 (March 11, 1999) freezing deposits for one year. An independent Spanish-language source (eldiario.ec) states verbatim that "the freezing affected more than one million people," matching the description exactly. The crisis is well documented as compounded by the 1997-98 El Niño flooding and the 1998 oil price collapse (Ecuador is oil-dependent), and it culminated in President Mahuad's announcement of dollarization on January 9, 2000 — confirmed by multiple sources. All year, actors, magnitudes, and sequence in the description hold up under independent verification.

Banco del Progreso ('El Progreso') is explicitly confirmed by a contemporaneous press account as 'the nation's No. 2 bank' (Filanbanco being No. 1), and it closed its doors on March 22, 1999 — directly corroborating the 'second-largest bank' detail that most needed checking. The 1997-98 El Nino flooding (~13% of GDP cost per Wikipedia) and the 1998 oil price collapse are both independently confirmed as compounding factors. Dollarization was announced by Mahuad on January 9, 2000, exactly as stated. Overall: real event, correct country, correct year, and all central facts (actors, bank rankings, dates, mechanism, macro drivers, resolution) match documented history.

title: NEE-01 Pegaso Becomes Ecuador's First Satellite in Orbit
reason: Confirmed via Wikipedia and independently via eoPortal (European Space Agency-affiliated database): NEE-01 Pegaso, Ecuador's first satellite, was built by EXA (Ecuadorian Civilian Space Agency) for approximately $30,000, launched as a secondary payload on a Chinese Long March 2D rocket from Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center on 26 April 2013. It transmitted its first live video from orbit on 16 May 2013. On 23 May 2013 it had a close pass/glancing collision with debris from a 1985 Tsyklon-3 rocket upper stage, causing damage/uncontrolled rotation. A signal recovery effort (EXA received audio signal via the NEE-02 Krysaor satellite, confirmed by January 2014) verified Pegaso had survived the collision. All material details (country, year, actor, cost, launch vehicle, dates, debris incident, recovery) match the description exactly.

verifications.reason: All material details confirmed by multiple independent sources: NEE-01 Pegaso, a CubeSat built by Ecuador's EXA (Ecuadorian Civilian Space Agency) for about $30,000, was Ecuador's first satellite, launched as a secondary payload on a Chinese Long March 2D rocket from Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center on 26 April 2013. It transmitted its first live video from orbit on 16 May 2013. On 23 May 2013 it passed very close to debris from a spent 1985 Tsyklon-3 rocket upper stage over the Indian Ocean, suffering a 'glancing blow' that damaged/disabled it (declared lost 28 August 2013). On 25 January 2014, EXA recovered an audio segment of the Pegaso signal during a transmission from sister satellite NEE-02 Krysaor, confirming Pegaso had survived the collision. Every detail in the description (country, year, cost, builder, launch vehicle/date, first video date, collision date, 2014 recovery) matches the historical record exactly.
